title: Why Cats Knead: It May Start When They Were Kittens 🐱 (Things Living In Your House)
description:
Why do cats knead? International Cat Care says kittens treading with alternate front paws on the mother's abdomen helps stimulate the flow of milk. Emma Grigg, an animal behaviorist at the UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine, says kneading is most likely carried over from their days as kittens. If a cat kneads on your lap or chest, International Cat Care says this shows they associate your relationship with that of their mother when they were a kitten. On a favorite person or bed, Grigg says, it is a self-soothing behavior, and with humans it is almost like a sign of the bond. Some cats drool; a few adults retain the behavior. International Cat Care says kneading is a perfectly normal behavior, and cats should never be punished for it.
